top_story_title: Ransomware crews are still breaking into PAN-OS GlobalProtect through CVE-2026-0257
top_story_summary: Palo Alto Networks reports continuing exploitation of CVE-2026-0257 (CVSS 7.8), an authentication bypass in the GlobalProtect portal and gateway of PAN-OS, and in Prisma Access. The flaw comes from the firewall accepting cookies without detailed validation and integrity checking, which lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker bypass security restrictions and establish an unauthorised VPN connection. Palo Alto Networks patched it in May 2026; CISA added it to the KEV catalog on 2026-05-29 with a 2026-06-01 remediation due date and records it as used in ransomware operations.
top_actions: Inventory every GlobalProtect portal and gateway, plus Prisma Access tenants, and compare the running PAN-OS build against the vendor's fixed-release table - check the vendor advisory for the fixed release rather than assuming a build number.
Upgrade inside the change window, HA pair secondary first; where a window is not available yet, apply the mitigations Palo Alto Networks documents in its advisory.
After upgrade, terminate all active GlobalProtect sessions and revoke session cookies and tokens - the vulnerability abuses cookie handling, so stolen cookies must be assumed.
Rotate local admin credentials, API keys, device certificates and VPN pre-shared keys on every affected firewall; a pre-patch compromise survives the upgrade.

Hunt back to June: VPN logins with no matching MFA event, sessions from unexpected ASNs or geographies, new local accounts, unexpected outbound connections from the firewall, and configuration changes outside change records.
executive_summary: CVE-2026-0257, the PAN-OS GlobalProtect authentication bypass patched in May 2026 and listed in CISA KEV since 2026-05-29, is still being exploited by Qilin and Inc ransomware operators; exploitation is reported as far back as June.

A public proof-of-concept now exists for CVE-2026-106173 (CVSS 9.4), an unauthenticated path-traversal code execution flaw in Fortinet FortiSIEM - a platform that typically holds privileged credentials for the network estate.
Cisco patched a blind SQL injection in the Unified Intelligence Center web management interface; exploitation requires valid credentials and there are no workarounds.

Autonomous AI agents were used to attack more than 1,200 websites with minimal operator involvement - no network-device exploitation reported, but a reminder that exposed management surfaces are enumerated continuously.
No vendor AI-defence capability was announced or described in this cycle's items.
key_actions: **Palo Alto Networks** — Compare the running PAN-OS build on every GlobalProtect portal and gateway against the vendor's fixed-release table; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release.
**Palo Alto Networks** — Schedule the upgrade in the change window, HA pair secondary first; apply the vendor's documented mitigations in the meantime.
**Palo Alto Networks** — Confirm the patch state of both on-premises PAN-OS firewalls and Prisma Access tenants; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release and the tenant-side remediation steps.
**Palo Alto Networks** — Revoke active sessions and rotate service-account credentials and secrets stored on or used by the remote-access service after remediation.

**Fortinet** — Identify FortiSIEM supervisors, workers and collectors from the asset inventory and apply the Fortinet fixed release; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release and the upgrade order between node roles.
**Fortinet** — Remove the FortiSIEM web interface and collector ports from any internet-facing path immediately; restrict access to a management VLAN reached through a jump host.
**Palo Alto Networks** — Use the vendor threat brief as the authoritative source for indicators and mitigation steps, and re-read it before closing the incident - it is being updated.
**Palo Alto Networks** — Map the named operators' post-access tradecraft to existing detections for lateral movement from the firewall segment.

headlines.title: Ransomware gangs have been exploiting Palo Alto GlobalProtect VPN flaw since June
headlines.summary: Ransomware groups have exploited CVE-2026-0257, an authentication bypass in PAN-OS GlobalProtect, since June against healthcare, education, government and energy targets.

headlines.title: Qilin and INC Ransomware Groups Exploit Palo Alto Networks Flaw to Bypass MFA
headlines.summary: Palo Alto Networks says Qilin and INC ransomware operators are still exploiting CVE-2026-0257 in PAN-OS and Prisma Access to stand up VPN sessions that bypass MFA.

headlines.title: Critical FortiSIEM Flaw Gets Public Exploit PoC for Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
headlines.summary: A public proof-of-concept exploit now exists for CVE-2026-106173, an unauthenticated path-traversal code execution flaw rated CVSS 9.4 in Fortinet FortiSIEM.

headlines.title: Threat Brief: Active Exploitation of PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 (Updated October 20)
headlines.summary: Unit 42's threat brief on PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257, updated 20 October, attributes active exploitation to the Qilin and Inc ransomware operations.

headlines.title: Cisco Unified Intelligence Center SQL Injection Vulnerability
headlines.summary: Cisco released updates for a blind SQL injection in the Unified Intelligence Center web management interface that lets an authenticated local user read the internal database.
